name: Coordinating Interior Painting With Other Trades in a Los Angeles Remodel

mainEntity.name: What is the best way to coordinate interior painting with other remodeling work in a Los Angeles County home to avoid delays and rework?
mainEntity.text: What is the best way to coordinate interior painting with other remodeling work in a Los Angeles County home to avoid delays and rework?

acceptedAnswer.text: To avoid delays and costly repainting in a Los Angeles County remodel, interior painting must be slotted at the right stage of the project. Generally, painting should start after demolition, framing, rough electrical and plumbing, major drywall work, and most flooring are complete. This ensures surfaces are stable and reduces the chance that other trades will damage fresh paint. However, final painting often happens before installing delicate fixtures, decorative lighting, and hardware so these items do not need to be masked or risk overspray. If you are adding new baseboards or crown molding, have them installed and caulked before painters begin finishing coats, although priming can happen earlier. In Los Angeles, where contractor schedules book out weeks in advance, it is smart to involve your painter early in the planning, share your critical path schedule, and reserve a flexible start window. Ask how they prefer to sequence with cabinet installers, tile setters, and flooring contractors, especially when doing staircases or open-plan spaces. Build at least a few buffer days around painting to accommodate inevitable delays from other trades. Also, clarify who handles touch-ups after punch-list items like additional outlet cuts or fixture moves. A well-timed painting phase keeps your remodel moving and prevents paying twice to fix avoidable damage.
